title: Sunny and the Crescent Moon
description: Little Sonny the quokka sees the crescent moon for the first time and wonders about all the things it watches over. A quiet, wonder-filled bedtime story for little ones. Part of Sonny's Cozy Quokka Bedtime Tales.
narration:
Sunny woke up very early — much earlier than usual.

The sky outside was still dark, but a different kind of dark than nighttime. Softer. With a faint line of deep blue at the edge of the trees.

He padded outside and looked up.

And there it was.

A crescent moon.

Just a thin, bright curve of white light hanging in the dark blue sky. Like someone had taken a small piece of moonlight and held it up very carefully for everyone to see.

Sunny stared at it for a long time.

He thought about how the moon was so far away. So much further than the top of the tallest tree, or the end of the biggest sky he could see. And still — still — he could see it clearly. So bright. So patient.

He wondered what the moon could see from up there.

All the sleeping animals in their burrows and hollows. All the nests tucked into branches. All the little creeks running quietly in the dark. All the children, just like Sunny, perhaps — tucked into their beds, breathing slowly, dreaming.

He thought the moon must feel very fond of all of it.

Sunny sat down in the cool grass and watched the crescent moon until it began to fade, gently, as the sky grew lighter.

The birds began to wake. One clear note, then another.

The moon grew softer and softer, until it was barely a trace in the morning blue.

But Sunny knew it was still there.

Goodnight, little Sunny. Goodnight, crescent moon. Goodnight, everything sleeping beneath the soft and watching sky.
